# To my friends, neighbours, Little Acorns families, and everyone who has reached out

First, I’m safe. I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch, and Marmalade is safe too. Everyone got out of our block. If you’ve been waiting for a reply from me since Saturday night, I’m so sorry to have left you worrying.

My phone has hardly stopped, and I’ve been crying at just about every message. I’m grateful, but I’m also exhausted, and I don’t have the energy to tell the story over and over or answer everyone individually. I thought it would help to put everything in one place: what happened, what I need, and where to find the fundraiser that is actually ours.

Please feel free to forward this letter. There is also an unrelated fundraiser being circulated in my name, so I especially want the correct information to reach anyone who might be thinking of donating.

## What happened

At around 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory. I live in flat 12, on the second floor.

My neighbour, Uncle Faizel, banged on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers. That’s how I woke up. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade, and nothing else.

Everyone from the block’s 14 flats got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and were sent home. I’m very relieved to be able to say that.

The fire department has said it was probably an electrical fault, but the investigation is still ongoing. I don’t know any more than that, and I don’t want to guess or pass on rumours.

My flat has extensive smoke and water damage, and the lounge ceiling came down. The landlord says nobody can move back in for at least six weeks. I don’t yet know what, if anything, I’ll be able to save.

That’s the short version, and it’s about as much as I can manage to write about the fire itself right now. Please understand if I don’t want to go through all the details when we speak.

Marmalade hid under a car for two hours afterwards, which was its own kind of awful, but she is safe now. Furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t.

## Thank you

Some of you have sent messages. Some have offered beds, lifts, money, clothes, or help with things I haven’t even had the headspace to think about yet.

One of my children’s moms dropped a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday. She didn’t even knock. She just left it there. I don’t really have words for how much that meant.

And Uncle Faizel: thank you. I keep thinking about you going from door to door.

To everyone who has helped, please know that I have noticed, even when I haven’t replied. A quiet phone on my side does not mean your message hasn’t mattered. People have been so good to me, and I’m struggling to take it all in.

I hate asking for help. I feel strange about having a fundraiser at all. Zinhle’s response was, more or less, “Shut up and accept it.” So I’m trying to do that, and to be clear about what would actually help rather than saying “I’m fine” when things aren’t fine yet.

## What I need at the moment

**Help with a deposit for a new place.** This is my biggest practical need. I have somewhere safe to stay for now, thanks to my sister, but I need to work out what comes next.

**Shoes for work, size 6, and work clothes, size 34.** I have enough general clothing now, but I could still use suitable things for being back in the classroom.

**A working laptop.** If anyone has an older laptop they no longer use, I would be very grateful. It doesn’t need to be new or fancy. All my lesson planning was on mine, and having something to work on would make a real difference.

Please don’t feel you need to buy something new or help in every way. These are just the specific things I’m trying to sort out.

## What I don’t need

For now, **please don’t send more general clothing or food**.

People have already been incredibly generous with clothes, and I have more than enough. I’ll pass the extras on to other people in the block who need them.

My sister’s freezer is also full. We are fed, I promise. Thank you to everyone who made sure of that.

I know sending something practical is often the easiest way to show you care. I’m only saying this so that nobody spends money unnecessarily, and so that help can go where it’s needed.

## The correct fundraiser — and a warning

Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy page for me. **This is the only fundraiser authorised by me:**

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**, and when I checked this morning, it had already reached **R11 400**. That is an enormous amount of kindness. Thank you to everyone who has contributed or shared the link.

There is also a page called **“Thandi Fire Relief”** being circulated elsewhere, along with a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money into a Capitec account.

**That is not my fundraiser. The Capitec EFT request is not from me. I have reported it. Please do not send money through either of those routes.**

If you’ve received that message, please let the person who sent it know, and send them this letter or Zinhle’s correct link instead. If you’re sharing the fundraiser, please copy the link above so there’s no confusion.

There is no pressure to donate. I know people have their own bills and worries. Sharing the correct information is helpful too.

## A note to my Little Acorns families

To the parents at Little Acorns Pre-Primary in Mowbray, and especially my Ladybirds families: **the concert on 27 November is still happening.**

The 22 crowns and the children’s handprint banner that I’d taken home to laminate are gone. That part hurts. But please don’t worry about the concert. The Ladybirds will have crowns.

I’m coming back to school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of my return in front of the children. I’m grateful for your concern, but I’d really appreciate being able to come in quietly and get on with our day. I don’t want the little ones worrying about me.

Finally, please bear with me. I’ll reply to comments slowly, and I may not manage to answer DMs. Please don’t be offended, and please don’t feel you need to send another message to check that I saw the first one.

I’m safe, I’m not alone, and I have people helping me work out the next steps. Thank you for giving me some room to breathe, and for being there.

With love and a very grateful heart,  
**Thandi**
